rationale: New sourced discrepancy on the decision-consumption path (A5). handleCommit (epaxos/epaxos.go:1066-1113) may create a placeholder instance via newInstanceDefault, whose lb field is nil, and then dereferences inst.lb.clientProposals at epaxos/epaxos.go:1092 with no nil check, when commit.Replica == r.Id and the commit carries a single NOOP command. handlePrepareReply guards exactly this placeholder state (it checks lb == nil before using it, epaxos/epaxos.go:1210), so the placeholder-with-nil-lb state is expected in this codebase and the guard's absence in handleCommit is a sourced asymmetry. If the event is legal the dereference panics in the replica's run goroutine (no recover in the message loop), removing a participant. The open premise is whether a NOOP Commit for the receiver's own row can be delivered while its local entry is a placeholder (created by newInstanceDefault or learned only through PreAccept/Accept, which never set lb). A NOOP command is produced by recovery restart: handlePrepareReply sub-cases 5/6 call startPhase1 with state.NOOP() when no reply carried commands (epaxos/epaxos.go:1307-1312), and bcastCommit then broadcasts that command with Replica set to the row owner. I am raising this as a Candidate, not a confirmed defect, because the fault history that leaves the row owner without its own instance is not yet sourced (the durability/restart path is unread). I also noted, as a separate observation, that handlePrepareReply itself evaluates lb := inst.lb before its inst == nil check (epaxos/epaxos.go:1206-1210); that is a different premise and is left for its own question.

feedback.answered: handleCommit dereferences inst.lb.clientProposals (epaxos/epaxos.go:1092) on the NOOP-repropose branch without checking inst.lb, although newInstanceDefault leaves lb nil and handlePrepareReply explicitly guards lb == nil for the same placeholder state. The reachable trigger would be a Commit carrying a single NOOP for the receiver's own row; NOOP commands are produced by the recovery restart path (epaxos/epaxos.go:1307-1312). Whether the row owner can hold a placeholder at that moment remains the open premise.
remaining: Whether a NOOP Commit for the receiver's own row can legally arrive while that receiver's instance is a placeholder (inst.lb == nil), which would turn the missing guard into a reachable panic.
Whether handlePrepareReply's lb := inst.lb before its inst == nil check (epaxos/epaxos.go:1206-1210) is reachable with a stale reply; separate question.
A1 fast-path qualification and A2 ballot/authority transitions still have no executed check.
The durability/restart replay path (A6) and membership/quorum-file selection (A4) remain unread.
feedback.rationale: Records a concrete, sourced crash-path asymmetry on the commit consumer, distinguishes the reachability premise that is still open, and keeps the analogous prepare-reply ordering issue as an independent unknown.

question.question: Can a Commit that carries a single NOOP for the receiver's own row reach handleCommit while the local instance is a placeholder with inst.lb == nil, so that the dereference inst.lb.clientProposals panics?
question.importance: Availability of a replica: an unhandled nil-pointer dereference inside handleCommit runs in the replica's message-processing goroutine with no recover, so a legal recovery-generated NOOP commit could crash a participant. Impact is loss of a participant (and possible loss of progress if repeated), not corruption of a decided value.
participants: row owner of the instance (commit.Replica == r.Id)
recovering coordinator that broadcast the NOOP commit
contexts: recovery restart with state.NOOP() when no Prepare reply carried a command (handlePrepareReply sub-cases 5/6)
replica that holds only a placeholder or a PreAccept/Accept-derived entry (never sets lb)
event_paths: handlePrepareReply sub-cases 5/6 -> startPhase1(state.NOOP()) -> commit -> bcastCommit with Replica = row owner
handleCommit: newInstanceDefault (lb nil) -> commit.Command is single NOOP -> inst.lb.clientProposals

supporting_behavior_ids.B-PREPARE-REPLY-LEADER: generates the NOOP command through the recovery restart sub-cases 5/6
supporting_behavior_ids.B-PHASE1: installs the command (NOOP) and the per-instance lb on the committing coordinator
supporting_behavior_ids.B-RECOVERY-START: creates the placeholder instance whose lb is nil on replicas that only learned the instance, and issues the Prepare that leads to the NOOP restart

counterevidence: handleCommit returns early when inst.Status >= COMMITTED or commit.Ballot < inst.bal; a fresh placeholder has Status NONE and bal -1, so neither guard prevents the dereference.
handlePrepareReply does guard lb == nil (epaxos/epaxos.go:1210), so the placeholder-with-nil-lb state is treated as expected elsewhere; the commit path omits the equivalent guard.
unknowns: Whether any fault history the run assumes delivers a NOOP Commit for the receiver's own row while its local entry is a placeholder (row owner lost the instance, or learned it only via PreAccept/Accept which do not set lb).
Whether the NOOP-repropose block can be entered with commit.Replica == r.Id in the same scenario, versus always being short-circuited by an earlier state.
question.trigger_rationale: A missing nil check before a pointer dereference is a direct crash if the event is legal, and the neighbouring handler's explicit lb == nil guard shows the placeholder state is expected, so the single remaining premise is the legal history that produces a NOOP commit for the receiver's own row.
